title: A document renders to a Page under a Format built with a builder
body:
Today `cmr::parse(markdown)` returns a `Document` holding `blocks` and `links`, and `Document::rows(width)` lays it out as a `Vec<Row>`, each row exactly `width` columns. Every other layout choice is left to the caller. coax makes several of them itself in its `ui.rs`:

- `wrap_code` sets `wrap` on every `Block::Code`
- `rule_tables` sets `rules` on every `Block::Table`
- `table_width` and `column_widths` cap table columns at 40 and squeeze them toward 16. `column_widths` finds the natural widths by laying a table out at 1000 columns and splitting cmr's drawn `─┼─` rule.
- `kept_whole` lays a wide code block out at its natural width so coax can pan it, assuming cmr's 2-column code gutter
- `markdown_popup_rows` cuts output to a number of rows and ends it with `…`

## Proposal

Three top-level types: `Document`, the parsed markdown; `Format`, how to lay it out and draw it; `Page`, the result.

```rust
let document = cmr::parse(TOP);
let page = document.render();

let column = Format::builder().width(30).height(8).build();
let left = cmr::parse(LEFT).render_with(column);
```

- `Document::render(&self) -> Page` is `self.render_with(Format::default())`.
- `Document::render_with(&self, Format) -> Page` replaces `Document::rows`.
- `Format` is `Copy`, has private fields, no `new()`, and a public `Default`. `Format::builder()` returns a `FormatBuilder`. Each setter takes and returns the builder, and `build()` returns the `Format`.
- `Page` holds the rows. `rows() -> &[Row]`, `string() -> String` with SGR codes and OSC 8 hyperlinks, `bytes() -> Vec<u8>`, and `Display`.

The first group of settings:

| setter | takes | default |
|---|---|---|
| `width` | `usize` | 80 |
| `height` | `usize`: pad short output, clip long output and end it with `…` | none, the natural height |
| `horizontal` | `Horizontal::{Left, Center, Right}`, where content narrower than the width sits | `Left` |
| `vertical` | `Vertical::{Top, Center, Bottom, Spread}`, where spare height goes. `Spread` shares it between blocks. | `Top` |
| `code` | `Overflow::{Wrap, Cut, Keep}` for code lines wider than the width. `Keep` lays the block out at its natural width. | `Cut` |
| `table_rules` | `bool`, a rule between body rows | `false` |
| `columns` | `RangeInclusive<usize>`, the floor and cap of a table column's width | today's behaviour |
| `gap` | `usize`, blank rows between blocks | 1 |

## Rejected

- A builder returned by `Document::format()` that holds the document. Nothing could name it: it was a layout and a document at once.
- `Layout` for the settings. It leaves out the visual ones, such as `table_rules`.
- Renaming the per-piece `Style` to free the name for the settings. A per-piece `Style` is what readers expect.
- Bit flags for alignment. They allow combinations like `Left | Center`, and they mixed the horizontal and vertical choices into one value.

## Out of scope

- `Row::links()`, which would give each link's row, column and width for clicks, and an `indent` setting. Both come after this group.
- Moving coax onto the new API, which is coax-550b84 in coax.

## Cost

Breaking, inside the 0.3.0 release that is already breaking. `Document::rows` goes away.
close_reason: Landed in f455382. The gaps coax found moving onto it are cmr-9f5a73, cmr-12acb4, cmr-79331f, cmr-1cd4b7, cmr-db5974, cmr-93655b and cmr-d8966f.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/c836bb27
notes.text:
Built, uncommitted. Choices the issue left open:

- `gap` applies between blocks at every level, inside quotes too. `Vertical::Spread` shares rows only among the gaps between top-level blocks, and the earlier gaps take the remainder. With one block it falls back to `Top`.
- A `Format` setting overrides a block only when it asks for something. Under `code(Cut)`, a block whose own `wrap` is true still wraps. A table gets rules when its own `rules` or `table_rules(true)` is set. The default `Format` lays out every block as before.
- Rendering lays the document out, then shifts it for `horizontal`, then pads or clips it to `height`. The padding rows and the `…` row are not shifted.
- Under `Overflow::Keep` a code block is laid out at the larger of the width and its longest line or language header, plus its gutter, so its rows can be wider than the width.
